quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If your car breaks down on a highway, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in your car and wait for help.
Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
Honk your horn at passing cars.
Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: Turn on your hazard flashers. Carefully exit the road and park as far off it as possible. Other drivers need to see you easily. Lift your hood to show your vehicle is disabled.

questions.question: You are driving on a divided highway with multiple lanes. You see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching. What should you do?

options.text: Ignore the signal if other lanes are available for the emergency vehicle.
Stop as quickly as possible.
Slow down, move to give the emergency vehicle a clear path, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to give the emergency vehicle a clear path, and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights, slow down. Move your vehicle to create a clear path and stop. Do not try to drive faster than the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, what should you do?

options.text: Take turns more slowly than normal.
Change lanes quickly.
Speed up.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take turns more slowly than normal.
questions.explanation: Driving too fast on slippery roads is dangerous, especially on turns and curves. Slow down more than you normally would when the road is wet or icy.

questions.question: What can cause distracted driving?

options.text: Eating, drinking, or smoking.
Talking or texting on a phone.
Changing a radio station or CD.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Drivers must focus fully on driving. Any activity besides driving takes your attention away and can create danger.

questions.question: What affects how far your vehicle travels before stopping?

options.text: How fast your vehicle is going.
The condition of your brakes and tires.
The condition of the road.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Braking distance is affected by your speed, the condition of your brakes and tires, and the condition of the road surface.

questions.question: When sharing the road with a truck, remember that trucks generally:

options.text: Need longer distances to stop than cars do.
Pass more quickly going downhill than cars do.
Turn in a smaller space than cars do.
Pass more quickly going uphill than cars do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need longer distances to stop than cars do.
questions.explanation: Because trucks are large and heavy, they need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles.

questions.question: What is the main concern with this sign?

options.text: Your headlights will not work properly if one side of your car is higher.
A tire could be damaged if you drift onto the shoulder.
Your car could hydroplane if there is water on the shoulder.
You could lose control of your vehicle if you drift onto the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: You could lose control of your vehicle if you drift onto the shoulder.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the shoulder is lower than the road. If one wheel drops off the road, do not brake hard or turn sharply. This could cause you to lose control.

questions.question: Where must you keep proof of liability insurance?

options.text: At your workplace.
In a bank safety deposit box.
In your vehicle while driving.
At your neighbor's house.

questions.correctAnswerText: In your vehicle while driving.
questions.explanation: The law requires you to carry proof of liability insurance in your vehicle. If an officer asks to see it and you cannot provide it, you will get a ticket.

questions.question: If you drive while intoxicated and injure or kill someone, what could happen?

options.text: You will only pay a fine.
You will only go to jail.
You will only lose your license.
You could lose your license and go to jail.

questions.correctAnswerText: You could lose your license and go to jail.
questions.explanation: Driving while intoxicated is illegal and dangerous. If you cause an accident that injures or kills someone, you may go to jail for two to seven years, pay a $5,000 fine, and lose your license for five years.

questions.question: What should you do if another driver is driving aggressively toward you?

options.text: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Follow closely behind them.
Make gestures to show you disapprove.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and create distance between yourself and the aggressive driver. Slow down and let them pass. Do not make eye contact or make rude gestures.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A left curve is ahead.
A series of curves is ahead.
An S-curve is ahead.
The road will be slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road will be slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that the road becomes slippery when it is wet.

questions.question: How can alcohol affect you while driving?

options.text: It slows your reaction time.
It gives you a false sense of confidence.
It affects your thinking ability.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time and harms your judgment, self-control, and balance. It also weakens your vision and ability to judge distance. Never drive after drinking alcohol.

questions.question: What does a "No right on red" sign mean?

options.text: You can turn right even if the light is red.
You cannot turn right when the light is red.
The intersection has many traffic crashes.
You do not have to stop at a red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn right when the light is red.
questions.explanation: Usually, you can turn right on red after a complete stop if the way is clear. However, when a "No right on red" sign is posted, you must not turn right at a red light.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn left.
No left turn.
No U-turn.
Truck route to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: No left turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means left turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What problems do worn or bald tires cause?

options.text: They make turning more difficult.
They are more likely to hydroplane.
They increase your stopping distance.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Worn or bald tires increase stopping distance, make turning harder, and increase the risk of hydroplaning. Always check your tires and replace them when they are worn.

questions.question: When you see a school bus stopped with its stop arm extended, what should you do?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait.
Honk your horn before passing on the left.
Keep driving when you think children are done exiting.
Pass the bus before its door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait.
questions.explanation: You must stop completely when you see a school bus with its stop arm extended. Do not proceed until the stop arm is pulled in.

questions.question: What is the purpose of highway markings?

options.text: They are usually not important.
They are only found in construction zones.
They give information to drivers.
They are usually red and blue.

questions.correctAnswerText: They give information to drivers.
questions.explanation: Highway markings help drivers stay in the correct position, show safe passing zones, and warn about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What happens when drivers drink alcohol before driving?

options.text: They are always aware of the risks.
They lose control over their body, mind, and vehicle.
They become better drivers because they are more careful.
They have faster reaction times.

questions.correctAnswerText: They lose control over their body, mind, and vehicle.
questions.explanation: Alcohol harms judgment, vision, focus, and reaction time. Never drink any amount of alcohol before driving.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on major highways?

options.text: Stay alert.
Keep your eyes moving.
Be ready to react to hazards.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stay alert on highways and be ready to react quickly. Keep your eyes moving and avoid looking at one thing for more than a few seconds to prevent highway hypnosis.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is driving aggressively behind you?

options.text: Get out of the aggressive driver's way.
Stare at the driver while they pass.
Speed up while they are passing.
Block the passing lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of the aggressive driver's way.
questions.explanation: If an aggressive driver is behind you, move out of their way. Do not make eye contact or challenge them by speeding up, as this may make them angrier and more dangerous.

questions.question: What should you do to make sure your physical condition does not make you an unsafe driver?

options.text: Stay physically fit and get regular check-ups.
Understand how any medicine you take affects your driving.
Drive only within your physical limits.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Your physical condition affects how safely you can drive. You should know your physical limits and only drive when it is safe.

questions.question: When should you not pass another vehicle?

options.text: On a hill or curve.
When a school bus has its red lights flashing.
When you are approaching an intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Never pass if you cannot see clearly ahead, if there is an oncoming vehicle, at an intersection, at a railroad crossing, on a bridge, or in any no-passing zone. Do not pass a school bus with flashing red lights unless you are on the opposite side of a divided road.

questions.question: Anything that requires you to ____ could cause you to crash.

options.text: Take your eyes off the road
Take your hands off the wheel
Take your attention away from driving
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that makes you take your attention away from driving, take your eyes off the road, or take your hands off the wheel.

questions.question: What should you do to change lanes safely?

options.text: Check your mirrors and signal, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot in the direction you want to move, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, and change lanes.
Signal and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot in the direction you want to move, then change lanes.
questions.explanation: To change lanes safely, turn on your signal first. Check your rearview and side mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot in the direction you want to move. Make sure no one else is entering that lane. Change lanes only when it is safe.

questions.question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: Drink coffee.
Exercise.
Give your body time to process the alcohol.
Take a cold shower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give your body time to process the alcohol.
questions.explanation: Only time can reduce your BAC. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers cannot lower your BAC or make you sober. They may help you stay awake, but they do not change your BAC.
